fields.h1: Build an Event Waiver Form Signed Before Anyone Joins In
fields.hero_description: Build an event waiver form that collects a signature from every attendee, guardian, and walk-up before the event starts.
fields.features_heading: Signatures Collected Before the Event Starts
fields.features_subheading: These six pieces put the event waiver form inside registration, the group invite, and the check-in table at the gate.
fields.feature_1:
Clauses that follow the activities

Attendees pick their activities first, and the waiver adds a clause to initial for each one. Someone who came only for the food trucks reads the general release and signs.
fields.feature_2:
A guardian section for anyone under 18

A date of birth under 18 opens a section for the guardian's name, phone number, and signature. The guardian's signature is saved on the minor's own record, not on a separate sheet.
fields.feature_3:
One link for a whole group

Organizers share a single link with a team, a class, or an office. Each person signs for themselves, and the organizer sees a roster with Signed or Waiting beside every name.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders before the event

Two days out, anyone on a roster without a signature gets an email reminder. The organizer hears by email or in Slack once the last person on the roster has signed the waiver.
fields.feature_5:
A check-in screen for the gate

Gate staff type a last name on a tablet and see Signed with the date and time. A walk-up without a signature scans a QR code at the gate and signs on a phone while in line.
fields.feature_6:
Signed records you can take with you

Every signed waiver is a row in a database you own, searchable by name and event. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep building it there.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Signs, and When, at Four Events
fields.tab_content_1:
One link in the invite, 23 of 26 signed by Thursday

Hessel Robotics is taking 26 employees to Stonecrop Ropes Course on Friday. Office manager Brigitta Sandahl puts one waiver link in the calendar invite, and each coworker signs for themselves. By Thursday at noon, 23 have signed. The other 3 get an email reminder, and Brigitta gets the count by email.
fields.tab_content_2:
Two players signed for in a single submission

Every player at the Marrowind Spring Cup, a youth soccer tournament, needs a guardian's signature. Delphine Okoro registers her son Ezra, 9, and her daughter Noemi, 12, in one submission and signs once. Each child gets a separate record, so Ezra reads Signed on the U10 roster and Noemi on the U13 roster.
fields.tab_content_3:
Two clauses to initial, one for each activity picked

Everyone at the Bramblewick Harvest Festival signs the general release. Tomas Brandvold also picks the zip line and the climbing wall when he registers, so his waiver adds a clause for each, and he initials both before he signs. The hayride adds no clause. His record lists both activities with his initials beside each.
fields.tab_content_4:
Any walk-up who scans the gate code signs in line

Walk-ups at Sawgrass Obstacle Day arrive without a signed waiver. A sign at the gate carries a QR code that opens the waiver on their own phone. Isadora Pickett scans it and signs in line at 9:12 AM. The volunteer on the check-in tablet types Pickett, sees Signed, and hands her a wristband.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Event Waiver Form
fields.howto_description: Follow these seven steps to plan an event waiver form, put it into registration, and test check-in before the gates open.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask an attorney to review the release
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Put the waiver where people register
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every activity at the event, from the zip line to the food tent. Mark the ones with a risk that deserves its own clause. The general release covers everyone, and each risky activity adds one short clause to initial.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Have a local attorney write or review the general release and each activity clause before anyone signs. Enforceability depends on how the waiver is written and the laws of your state. Settle the wording before the form goes out.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for the date of birth near the top. Anyone under 18 then sees the guardian section right away. Decide whether one guardian may sign for several children in one submission, with a separate record saved for each child.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Make the waiver the last step of registration, put one shared link in group invites, and print a QR code for a sign at the gate. Name the person who follows up with anyone still unsigned.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write one prompt with the clauses, the guardian rule, and every place attendees sign. Emergent builds the event waiver form, the database behind it, and a tablet screen for checking people in. Ask in plain English when the event plan changes.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick when unsigned attendees hear about it, such as two days before the event and again that morning. Decide who learns when a group's roster is complete, and whether that note arrives by email or in Slack.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Sign in as a test walk-up
fields.howto_step_7_des: Scan the gate QR code with a phone, sign under a made-up name, and pick two activities. Then search that name on the check-in tablet and confirm it reads Signed, with both activity clauses initialed.
fields.hero_prompt: Build an event waiver form for my county fair that each attendee e-signs on a phone before getting a wristband at the gate.

faq_plan.q: What is an event waiver form?
faq_plan.a: An event waiver form is the document a participant signs before an event, acknowledging the risks of its activities and agreeing not to hold the organizer responsible if an injury or incident occurs. An event version names the event, its date, and the activities it covers.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an event waiver form?
faq_plan.a: List the activities, have an attorney settle the release wording, and decide where each attendee signs. Then describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. Emergent builds the form and the database that stores every signed waiver, and you change either one by prompting.

faq_plan.q: What should an event waiver form template include?
faq_plan.a: Start an event waiver form template with the event name, date, and location. Add the risks of each activity, then the release itself and a dated signature line. Ask for the participant's name, email, and date of birth, and a guardian signature line for minors. Emergent builds the same form from a plain-English description, with no response caps.

faq_plan.q: Should repeat attendees sign a new event waiver form for every event?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask for a new signature for each event, because the date, the location, and the activities change, and the waiver names all three. Have your attorney confirm the wording before you reuse a waiver across a series. For a place people visit every week, a gym waiver form signed once per membership is the closer fit.

faq_plan.q: How do I collect event waiver form signatures from a whole group?
faq_plan.a: Send one link to the whole group and have each person sign for themselves. An organizer who signs on behalf of 20 coworkers leaves 20 waivers nobody read. Ask the organizer for a headcount up front, and the roster shows how many signatures are still missing. The app Emergent builds saves each signature to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How should an event waiver form handle participants under 18?
faq_plan.a: Open a guardian section whenever the date of birth shows someone under 18, and ask for the guardian's own signature plus a number to reach them on the day. Some states limit the use of waivers for minors. Have your attorney review that section on its own before the event.

faq_plan.q: Can attendees sign an event waiver form on their phones at the gate?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Print the waiver link as a QR code on a sign by the entrance, and walk-ups sign while they wait in line. Keep each clause short enough to read on a small screen. A yoga waiver form for studio drop-ins works the same way, with the code taped beside the front desk.

faq_plan.q: How do I update an event waiver form after people have already signed it?
faq_plan.a: Save the new wording as a new version and ask everyone who signed the old one to sign again. Keep each signature tied to the version that person saw, with the date. Anyone who registers after the change sees only the new version.

faq_plan.q: How do I add activity-specific clauses to an event waiver form?
faq_plan.a: Ask attendees which activities they plan to join before the release, then show a short clause for each one they pick, with a box for their initials. Activities with no added risk carry no clause. Save the picks on the record, and staff at the zip line can check who initialed its clause.

faq_plan.q: How do I find a signed event waiver form after the event?
faq_plan.a: Search the records by the attendee's name or the event, then open the one with the signature, the date, and any initialed clauses. Keep the records for as long as your attorney or insurer advises. A salon waiver form uses the same lookup when a client calls about a past appointment.

plan.angle: The searches behind event waiver form are organizers looking for wording and a way to collect it; template sites stop at the wording. This page shows the organizer how the form runs at four kinds of events: a company outing signed through one shared link with reminders, a youth tournament where one guardian signs for two players, a festival where each paid activity adds a clause to initial, and a gate where walk-ups sign on their own phones before a wristband. Release wording goes to the organizer's attorney; the e-signature is a record of who signed what and when.
